clue.text: Equal to bargains commonly grown by the farmer

parts.note: to be on par with something is to be equal to it
a snip is a colloquial word for a bargain, so bargains in common speech are snips

explanation.surface: Something matching a cheap deal is raised by a farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks SNIPS as informal speech for bargains.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsnips are root vegetables that farmers cultivate in their fields.

clue.text: Do your best to forget having this malady? Quite the contrary!

definitions.text: Do your best to forget having this malady? Quite the contrary!

parts.words: Do your best to forget having this malady? Quite the contrary!
parts.note: the illness in question is not one you try to forget about having; it is the one that makes you forget everything

explanation.surface: A wry remark about trying to put an illness out of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is the condition that does the forgetting for you, the reverse of the surface advice.

clue.text: A fall in winter temperatures

parts.note: reads like a weather report of the thermometer dropping, but the fall is of precipitation that comes down in cold weather

explanation.surface: A forecaster notes the thermometer dropping in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-frozen rain is a kind of precipitation, a fall, seen when winter is cold.

clue.text: We take offence if it's offered to us!

definitions.text: We take offence if it's offered to us!

parts.words: We take offence if it's offered to us!
parts.note: something offered usually pleases, but this thing when offered gives offence, an affront

explanation.surface: A touchy group explaining what upsets them.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront or slight is precisely what people take offence at when it is given.

clue.text: Fight. Where you might do it, and what you'd be doing

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do in practice
boxers fight in a ring

explanation.surface: A three-part riddle about a boxing bout: the action, the venue and the activity.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces build the word, and the whole clue's last phrase is the definition: practising boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxing practice bouts are the activity a fighter is engaged in while in the ring.

clue.text: This Caucasian sergeant was in the air

definitions.text: This Caucasian sergeant was in the air

parts.words: This Caucasian sergeant was in the air
parts.note: Caucasian means white, so the White Sergeant of a well-known Scottish country dance and tune, whose title adjective is the word wanted; in the air means in the tune

explanation.surface: A soldier from the Caucasus apparently taking flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Dashing White Sergeant' is a Scottish reel and song; 'Caucasian' stands in for White and 'air' means a tune, not the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective in the dance title describes the white sergeant, meaning stylish and spirited.

clue.text: Forces pin-up girl? No, but model accepted to represent the regiment

definitions.text: Forces pin-up girl? No, but model accepted to represent the regiment

parts.words: Forces pin-up girl? No, but model accepted to represent the regiment
parts.note: the model is not a pin-up but an accepted norm, and the same word names the flag carried to represent a regiment

explanation.surface: A soldiers' favourite pin-up model is passed over for a regimental mascot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' and 'pin-up girl' suggest a glamour model; the model here is an accepted benchmark, and a regiment's flag is its standard too.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an accepted benchmark and a regimental flag or banner.

clue.text: Hides their raw materials

parts.note: hides looks like a verb about concealing, but it is the plural noun for animal skins, the stock in trade of leather workers

explanation.surface: Someone conceals their stock of raw materials.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather makers work animal skins, hides, into leather, so hides are their raw material.

clue.text: It stars various show business personalities

indicators.note: various suggests the letters arranged in different ways, so these words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A film boasts a varied cast of showbiz celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges the letters of IT STARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers and entertainers are personalities of show business.

clue.text: Not driving hints in the paper, but a column for the motorist

definitions.text: Not driving hints in the paper, but a column for the motorist

parts.words: Not driving hints in the paper, but a column for the motorist
parts.note: column suggests a newspaper motoring column, but it is the shaft in a car that carries the wheel

explanation.surface: A newspaper's motoring column, not a driving-tips feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The column is the car part on which the wheel sits, not a newspaper feature.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the mechanism that turns a car, as in the column holding the wheel.

clue.text: Better to get back the result of his calculations!

definitions.text: Better to get back the result of his calculations!

parts.words: Better to get back the result of his calculations!
parts.note: better is one who bets; at a bookmaker's a clerk works out the payout the punter receives

explanation.surface: Advice that it is preferable to have someone's sums returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is not 'preferable' but a person who bets; the bookmaker's clerk who calculates winnings is called a settler.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker's clerk who calculates the returns owed on winning bets has this job title.

clue.text: Made by people in a row, so to speak

definitions.text: Made by people in a row, so to speak

parts.words: Made by people in a row, so to speak
parts.note: people in a row suggests sitting in a line, but a row is a quarrel, and quarrelling people make a din

explanation.surface: Something produced by people lined up together.
explanation.definitionFit: A din or racket is what people produce in a loud quarrel.

clue.text: Looks like a verbal examination that's gone by, concerning shepherds

parts.note: something that has gone by is in the past
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A past spoken test seems to be about sheep farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral life and poetry concern shepherds and the countryside.

clue.text: Woman who fought for a flower

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth these were a race of female warriors
read as flow-er, something that flows: a great South American river

explanation.surface: A woman warrior fought for a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is not a bloom but a thing that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both the female warriors of myth and the huge river of Brazil.

clue.text: Where the slanderer is when not at home and not in town!

parts.note: someone not at home is out
a slanderer tells untruths, so is engaged in lying

explanation.surface: Joking about where a slanderer can be found when away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote, outlying places are distant from the town centre.

clue.text: Is put at risk, being green and new

indicators.note: new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters before it

explanation.surface: Something is endangered because it is inexperienced and fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the letters of GREEN AND.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose to danger is to imperil or put at risk.

clue.text: In the main, stopped being hooked on the bed

definitions.text: In the main, stopped being hooked on the bed

parts.words: In the main, stopped being hooked on the bed
parts.note: the main is the sea; a ship stopped by its hook gripping the seabed

explanation.surface: Someone stopped being addicted to staying in bed, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly' but means at sea, and the bed is the seabed where the hook holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored ship is held stationary by its hook biting into the sea floor.

clue.text: Makes things less slack for giants, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word sounds like the one required

parts.note: Titans were giants of Greek myth

explanation.surface: Something tensed up on behalf of huge figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' signals that TITANS, giants, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw something tauter is to make it less slack.

clue.text: Old lover to irritate a worker

parts.note: to gall is to vex or irritate
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: An old flame annoys a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant was an old word for a suitor or ladies' man.

clue.text: To be in contact, a number enlist

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
to enlist is to join up

explanation.surface: Several people sign up so as to keep in touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that adjoin are next to each other and touching.

clue.text: Make inroads into decrees

indicators.note: make tells us to create something new from the letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Encroach on orders and rulings.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to order officially, to decree.

clue.text: Says yes, making an eager Pole delirious

indicators.note: delirious means wildly confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the South Pole

explanation.surface: A keen Polish person, in a frenzy, says yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delirious' rearranges EAGER plus S (Pole); 'Pole' looks like a Polish person.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent or assent is to say yes.

clue.text: Race to pass something on

definitions.meaning: a team race where runners take turns
to transmit or hand on a message

explanation.surface: Running to hand something over.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a team race with a baton and to transmit a message.

clue.text: She was made up by him!

definitions.text: She was made up by him!

parts.words: She was made up by him!
parts.note: She is the title of an adventure novel; made up means invented by its author, H. Rider, not wearing cosmetics

explanation.surface: A woman had her make-up done by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is H. Rider Haggard's 1887 novel; 'made up' means invented, not cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist wrote the novel She, so he invented its heroine.

clue.text: He can only be satisfied in part!

definitions.text: He can only be satisfied in part!

parts.words: He can only be satisfied in part!
parts.note: satisfied in part sounds like partly content, but a player is happy only when given a role in a play

explanation.surface: A man who is never fully contented.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer on stage needs a role, a part, to be happy.

clue.text: He's instructed to take charge of his own vehicle

definitions.text: He's instructed to take charge of his own vehicle

parts.words: He's instructed to take charge of his own vehicle
parts.note: a person having driving lessons is taught to control a car

explanation.surface: A man is told to look after his car.
explanation.definitionFit: A driving pupil is being taught to handle a car himself.

clue.text: Ten, about to take intoxicating drink and weave

indicators.note: about suggests the letters turned around and rearranged

parts.note: wine is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Ten people about to drink and then weave about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' rearranges TEN into ENT; 'to take' joins it to WINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist together or interlace is to weave strands.

clue.text: Lock Sid out first, causing suffering

indicators.note: first puts the rearranged name ahead of the other piece
out suggests the letters put out of order

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Locking Sid out first causes him pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' looks like a verb, shutting someone out, but it is a lock of hair; 'out' is the anagram signal and 'first' sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is anguish or great pain, suffering.
